newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany marks old Berlin Wall anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Germany marks old Berlin Wall anniversary.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl, marking the 36th anniversary of the building of the now extinct Berlin Wall, said on Tuesday it robbed millions of Germans of a future and would remain a symbol of repression.

Calling on Germans to recall the Wall in remaining vigilant while fighting extremism, Kohl said the communist regime of old East Germany built the Wall on August 13, 1961 "against the free will" of its citizens.
"By recalling the building of the Wall, we Germans can work actively to safeguard the values of freedom upon which our democracy is founded," Kohl said in a statement.
"Democrats agree to reject any kind of partnership with extremists. There can be no tolerance of intolerance."

The Berlin Wall, a 155-km (96-mile) cement and barbed wire barrier that surrounded West Berlin, sealed off the border between the city's East and West sectors for 28 years. It left the western half an enclave of democracy in the middle of communist East Germany.

Before it was opened in 1989, the Wall evoked the tense divide between Soviet and Western powers during the Cold War. The Wall's demise marked the collapse of East German communism, leading to German unification in 1990.

Peter Hintze, general secretary of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), called on Germans to ensure the last few slabs of the Wall remain standing as a memorial to those who were killed trying to escape to the West.

"The Wall was a monument to socialist oppression," Hintze said. "Today the remaining pieces of the Wall are a monument to freedom. I firmly commit myself to ensuring the rest of the Wall keeps standing in Berlin forever."
Berlin authorities have said 265 people were killed at the border between East and West Germany and at the Wall.
But evidence gathered by the independent August 13 Working Group suggests at least 916 people died trying to flee from the former communist East Germany.

Only a total of about two kilometres of the Wall are left standing in Berlin. Politicians, artists and families of victims are now fighting property developers to preserve the Wall's last remaining fragments.
